7787.stem:
The box-plot below shows the heights of students in Year 11 and Year 12 at a particular school.

\exfigure{708_q23_1}

figures.cap: box plots of heights of Year 11 and Year 12 students

parts.latex: What percentage of students in Year 11 have a height below 160 cm?
Find the interquartile range (IQR) for Year 11.
Are there any outliers for Year 11? Justify your answer with calculations.
There are the same number of students above 175 cm in Year 11 as there are students above 175 cm in Year 12. If there are 140 students in total in Year 11, how many students are in Year 12?

solutions.latex:
An outlier is a value below $Q_1 - 1.5 \times IQR$ or above $Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 - 1.5 \times IQR &= 160 - 1.5 \times 15 \\ &= 137.5 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR &= 175 + 1.5 \times 15 \\ &= 197.5 \end{aligned}$$
Outliers must be below $137.5$ or above $197.5$, so there are no outliers.
criteria: Finds one outlier boundary, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Box plot values read from the source working.

solutions.latex:
Above 175 cm in Year 11 is $25\%$ of the year.

Above 175 cm in Year 12 is $50\%$ of the year.

With 140 students in Year 11:
$$\begin{aligned} 25\% \text{ of Year 11} &= 0.25 \times 140 \\ &= 35 \text{ students} \end{aligned}$$
The numbers above 175 cm are equal, so $50\%$ of Year 12 is 35 students.

Hence there are 70 students in Year 12 in total.
$$\therefore\ \text{Year 12 has } 70 \text{ students}$$
criteria: Finds 35 students above 175 cm, or equivalent merit

708_q23_1.notes: Two horizontal box plots: Y11 148/160/168/175/195 and Y12 150/164/175/179/201. Boxes are grey-filled and every box-plot stroke is 0.9pt (rule 9). The Year 12 plot is black rather than the crop's grey, for consistency (rule 6). Faint grid with darker lines every 5, axis 145–205 with minor ticks, title centred over the plot (rule 20). Round 2 corrected the scale and moved 'Height (cm)' clear of the tick labels. What is left in the overlay is the faint grid and the scan's box fill.

7931.stem:
Chloe has collected the following $5$ point number summary:

\begin{itemize}
\item Lowest Score: $80$
\item $1^{\text{st}}$ Quartile: $85$
\item Median: $95$
\item $3^{\text{rd}}$ Quartile: $110$
\item Highest Score: $125$
\end{itemize}

parts.latex: Chloe claims that the highest score is an outlier. Is she correct? Justify your answer with suitable calculations.

solutions.latex:
A score is an outlier if $x > 1.5\times IQR + Q_3$.
$$\begin{aligned} 1.5\times 25 + 110 &= 147.5 \end{aligned}$$
Since $125 < 147.5$, the score $125$ is not an outlier.
$$\therefore\ \text{Chloe is wrong.}$$
criteria: Calculates the upper outlier boundary, or equivalent merit
